I was going to write a piece on ethics, but it struck me diving into that that I was going to have to provide some background, and that it was background that also applies to my views on rights and freedom, and which I erred by not posting before I posted that. So I'm posting it now. It underlies my views on rights and freedom, and my views on ethics/morality.

In a nutshell first - at most, individuals can only certainly control their own actions.

Some would argue that individuals can't even control that, and sooner or later I'll undoubtedly address that idea too, but in any event, the salient point is that *at most* we can only certainly control our own actions. We can manipulate or coerce or threaten or con or apply any of a staggering number of generally underhanded and destructive techniques to attempt to at least exert some measure of influence over the actions of others, but due to the simple and unavoidable facts of nature, we cannot directly control other people. No matter the extent to which we might manipulate another person, we simply cannot make that last leap and control their bodies and minds in the same sense in which we (at least appear to) control our own.

For this reason, I count all notions of rights, freedom, ethics, morality or what-have-you that demand or prohibit a course of action taken by another to be, at best, meaningless.

As I outlined in the piece on rights and freedom - if I assert that I have a right to life, that means that no other may deprive me of my life. However, the simple fact of the matter is that any other who is sufficiently determined and/or lucky CAN in fact deprive me of my life, and it doesn't matter how sound my arguments for my right to life might be. In the end, those arguments - that presumed right - is utterly meaningless, since it does not in fact constrain the actions of others. But if, on the other hand, I assert that YOU have a right to life, that means that I may not deprive YOU of your life. And that's something that's entirely within my power to do. Or, more broadly, my views regarding YOUR actions are irrelevant - only my views regarding MY actions are meaningful. And again, for the simple reason that I cannot control your actions - I can only control my own.

As I was about to get into - this also applies to ethics and morality. I can decree that such and such a course of action is wrong, but that does not in any way grant me the ability to prevent YOU from pursuing that course of action. Most believe that it grants them a justification for attempting to do so, but the simple fact of the matter is that it does not and cannot grant them the ability to actually do so, and again, for the quite simple reason that it's literally impossible to fully control the actions of another individual. But, just as with rights and freedom, one can (apparently) control ones own actions, so just as with rights and freedom, the only meaningful application of ethics and morality is on ones own actions. Just as with my example in the preceding paragraph - if I decree that stealing is morally wrong and therefore YOU should not do it, that's ultimately meaningless, since you can simply choose to go ahead and do it anyway. My decree has accomplished absolutely nothing - it's just empty words. However, if I decree that stealing is wrong and therefore I should not do it, that is actually within my power to make reality. I actually possess the power to accomplish that.

So, in my estimation, the only views on any such concepts regarding human behavior - rights, freedom, ethics, morality, so on - that are possibly meaningful are those that one uses to guide ones own behavior. Those that one seeks to apply to the behavior of others are ultimately meaningless, since they cannot serve to actually constrain the behavior of another.

Now... on to ethics and morality...
